text: The current crisis in the shelter system has been created by a lack of a wide range of affordable housing in Toronto. With almost 7,000 people sleeping in shelters, respite centres and drop-in centres each night, homelessness is on the rise and Toronto must concurrently build sufficient new shelter beds, deeply affordable housing, supportive, and transitional housing to accommodate this growth and to meet the 90 percent occupancy cap rate set out by City Council. Currently and for many years, occupancy levels regularly reach 97-100 percent, meaning those who need beds risk not being able to find them. However, the stark reality facing those without adequate homes is a multi-year wait for supportive housing and 181,000 people on the waitlist for affordable housing. City Council on March 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Director, Affordable Housing Office to work with the Deputy City Manager, Internal Corporate Services and in consultation with CreateTO, to conduct the necessary due diligence for the potential acquisition or expropriation of the property at 230 Sherbourne Street for affordable and/or supportive housing purposes, and to report to the Affordable Housing Committee at its June 25, 2018 meeting on the results of the due diligence, including negotiations with the property owner, and the potential sources of funding to acquire the property.
